sentences.text: In the Universal Century, not every mobile suit gets to be the hero's machine.
R-X zero N, the Banshee Norn, Goddess of Fate: the Earth Federation's second answer to the riddle of the Unicorn.
Like the Unicorn, she carries a psycho-frame, armor that answers a Newtype's will.
When the N-T-D system awakens, the mask splits, the frame burns green, and a machine of order starts to look disturbingly alive.
Her pilot is no chosen one. Riddhe Marcenas, a Federation ace, fighting for duty rather than destiny.
While Banagher rides the Unicorn toward answers, Riddhe is ordered to silence them.
The two machines were built as sisters. In the dark of space they do not simply fight. As the line goes: the Unicorn and the Banshee are pulling on each other.
And when the psycho-frame screams, it is not a curse. It was a prayer.
Near the end, sensors report resonance beyond every measurable limit, as if countless hearts were sounding at once.
She was built to bury the secret of Laplace.
In the end, even the Federation's sharpest spear could not stop the truth being born. We were blessed when we were born.
The Banshee Norn: the reluctant angel of the Universal Century.
